newsitem.title: DENMARK: BANG & OLUFSEN POSTS 11 PERCENT PROFIT GAIN.
newsitem.headline: BANG & OLUFSEN POSTS 11 PERCENT PROFIT GAIN.

text.p: Danish audio/video and television maker Bang & Olufsen said Wednesday its 1996-97 profit was up 11 percent from the prior year and its earnings should grow 15 percent in the year ahead.

"The result is as expected and exceeds our growth targets. The audio/video market in most European countries is still flat, so our result must be considered very satisfactory in that light," Bang & Olufsen said in a statement.

Bang & Olufsen reported pre-tax profit for the year 1996-97 of 321 million crowns ($45.2 million), compared to 1995-96's interim 272 million crowns ($38.3 million) and slightly lower than market analysts' expectations of an average 333 million crowns ($46.9 million).

It said its audio/video sales achieved solid growth in virtually all markets, at between 10 percent and 32 percent in Italy, Switzerland, the United States, the Netherlands, Belgium, Japan and Russia, aided by better agent and distribution networks.

It said its B&O Telecom unit, which produces mobile and cordless telephones, reported improved profits and turnover, while B&O Technology, which makes medical products, noted increased profits on unchanged sales.
